title: The brothers at the gate
hook: famine brings the brothers to Egypt, they don't recognize him, and he keeps his youngest brother with the cup in his bag

segments.voice: Yesterday: nafs, the self that pushes, notices, and can rest. Your line was I don't clear myself. Did you catch the self wanting to be right? Day sixty-seven.

Have you ever run into someone from years ago, someone who hurt you, and they didn't recognize you? You stood there, knowing everything, and they just saw a stranger. Yusuf is out of prison now. He asked the king to put him in charge of the storehouses, and the good years have come and gone. Now the hard years are here, just as he said. The hard years reach an old man and his sons in the land where Yusuf grew up. And one day, in the line of hungry travelers waiting for grain, Yusuf looks up and sees faces he'd know anywhere, his brothers. Today: the brothers at the gate.
screen: `OUT OF PRISON, OVER THE STORES.` → `THE FAMINE REACHES HOME.` → `FACES HE KNOWS IN THE LINE.`

segments.voice: Surah Yusuf, verse fifty-eight: they came in to him, and he knew them, and they did not know him. In Arabic, fa-'arafahum wa-hum lahu munkirun. The whole story in a line. The last time they saw him, he was a boy going down a well. Now he's the man who decides whether their family eats. He gives them their grain, generously. He even has their payment slipped back into their saddlebags. But he asks for one thing: next time, bring your youngest brother, your father's other son. Without him, don't come back. At home, Ya'qub doesn't want to let the youngest go. He's lost one son already on a trip with these brothers. In the end he makes them swear to bring him back and says: Allah is the best guardian. They return with the youngest, and Yusuf takes him aside and tells him quietly: I am your brother. Don't grieve over what they did. Then he has the king's drinking cup placed in that brother's bag. A herald shouts: you're thieves! The cup is found. And the brothers, under pressure, say something ugly: if he stole, well, a brother of his stole before. They mean Yusuf, to his face, without knowing it. And the Qur'an says Yusuf kept it in his heart and did not reveal it to them. He just thought: you're in a worse place than that. Why keep his brother? Commentators say it was a way, permitted to him, to keep the youngest safe with him. And a test. Would the brothers abandon another of their father's beloved sons, the way they once did? We'll see tomorrow.
screen: `HE KNEW THEM; THEY DIDN'T.` · `BRING YOUR YOUNGEST BROTHER.` · `I AM YOUR BROTHER.` · `THE CUP IN THE BAG.` · then, large: `HE KEPT IT IN HIS HEART.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: be generous to someone who hurt you. Settle, and breathe. Think of someone who once wronged you, not the deepest wound, something you can hold. Picture them in front of you, not knowing everything you know. Now picture giving them something anyway. Their full portion. A fair word. A favor they don't expect. Not because what they did was fine. Because you'd like to be the kind of person who fills the sacks. Notice what that does in your chest. If you pray, you can ask for good for them. The bell holds the time.
The brothers at the gate. Hungry travelers, and the brother they threw away, who knew them when they didn't know him. Today's word.
screen: `THE BROTHERS AT THE GATE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: he knew them. If someone who hurt you crosses your path today, give them their full portion, and keep the rest in your heart. Day sixty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims read Yusuf's generosity to his brothers as a model of restraint and kindness toward those who have done wrong, and Ya'qub's words, Allah is the best guardian, are often repeated when entrusting loved ones to Allah.

original.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 12:58: "he knew them, and they did not know him."

trapdoor: what you thought: Yusuf was getting his revenge.
what it means: he feeds the brothers who threw him away, keeps their insult to himself, and quietly brings his youngest brother close.
what a scholar hears: the cup has two names, siqaya (12:70) and suwa' al-malik (12:72); commentators say keeping the brother this way was a plan Allah allowed him (12:76).

notes: 12:54–79 paraphrased, not quoted. The index hook names Binyamin; the Qur'an calls him only 'his brother' / 'your brother from your father'. The script says 'youngest brother' and keeps the name out of the voice.
The voice says 'another of their father's beloved sons' rather than naming Rahil (Rachel), whom the Qur'an does not name.
12:77's 'a brother of his stole before': commentators give various accounts of what incident the brothers meant; the script does not explain it.
Keeping the brother as a plan permitted by Allah (12:76, 'kadhalika kidna li-Yusuf'): stated as commentary. Confirm.
No place name is given for the family's home (tradition says Canaan; the Qur'an mentions 'the desert', 12:100).
Close teases day 68 without teaching the forgiveness.

Review pass: 'ten' brothers is from tradition and Genesis, not stated in the Qur'an, so the voice no longer counts them; 'famine spreads beyond Egypt' softened to 'the hard years reach' the family (the Qur'an implies it through their journey, 12:58, 12:88). howItsDone reworded so 'Allah is the best guardian' is clearly Ya'qub's (12:64) and not in quotation marks.
Order check: in 12:64 Ya'qub says Allah is the best guardian before the oath in 12:66; the voice compresses this as 'makes them swear ... and says'. Acceptable paraphrase; confirm.
